name: Lydon's Toxin
summary: In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon has made a toxin to disrupt Venture Company logging in the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde adventurers carry it to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, who must find a way to spread it.

sections.title: A Royal Apothecary Solution
sections.body:
Apothecary Lydon made the toxin in the Hillsbrad Foothills to hinder Venture Company loggers in the Stonetalon Mountains. He says it kills on contact and may pass from one target to another.

Before it can reach the goblins near Windshear Crag, the mixture must cross continents to Thunder Bluff. There, Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative, needs the raw toxin to devise a wide-dispersal device called the Toxic Fogger.

faq.q: What is Lydon's Toxin used for?
faq.answer: Apothecary Lydon made the toxin to disrupt Venture Company work around Windshear Crag. It kills on contact and may spread among the goblin laborers.
Apothecary Lydon is a Royal Apothecary Society member stationed in Tarren Mill, in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He makes virulent poisons and experimental compounds for Forsaken aims.

faq.q: Why does the toxin need to go to Thunder Bluff?
faq.answer: Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff needs the toxin because it cannot yet be spread widely. She studies regional flora and coordinates Society efforts in Kalimdor. She adapts the mixture into a portable fogging device.

faq.q: What happens after Zamah receives the toxin?
aliases: what does zamah do with the toxin
faq.answer: Apothecary Zamah turns the toxin into a pressurized aerosol device called the Toxic Fogger. An operative can use it to spread the toxin through the Venture Company's encampment.

angles.text: The transport of Lydon's Toxin shows how far the Royal Apothecary Society's network reaches. It coordinates field research between Lordaeron and Kalimdor, showing the Forsaken's usefulness to their allies.
Tauren welcome help against the Venture Company's destruction of nature. Yet the Royal Apothecary Society's chemical methods test their shamanic sensibilities.
